expectation: Nuclear stain in many nucleated cells. In gut it should be strongest in proliferating crypt epithelium and fade toward the surface, with endothelium and macrophages positive in the stroma. Signal should fill nuclei and spare the cytoplasm and lumen.
notes: Rb signal is as bright on the empty slide as on the tissue, with debris spots scattered off the tissue. In the crypt fields the nuclear rings are darker than the stroma and lumen around them, so the stain avoids nuclei instead of marking them. The bright tissue edge in A looks like edge glow.
observed: A: strong yellow haze over the slide and tissue alike, many bright spots off the tissue, a glow along the tissue edges, tile seams. B/C: diffuse haze; the crypt nuclear rings show up pale against brighter stroma and lumen. D: a few blurry blobs not clearly sitting on nuclei.
why: The signal is background haze, edge glow and debris, and it sits outside nuclei rather than in a distinct nuclear population.
